name: pencil
phrases: Your pencil has **zero lead** in it.
Your pencil has zero lead in it. It never did.
In the 1500s, a huge deposit of a **black mineral** was dug up.
In the fifteen hundreds, a huge deposit of a black mineral was discovered.
People thought it was **lead,** and the name stuck.
People thought it was a form of lead, and the name stuck.
It was really **graphite:** Greek for “to write.”
It was really graphite, a form of carbon. Its name comes from the Greek word for to write.
Graphite is built from **flat sheets** of carbon atoms.
Graphite is built from flat sheets of carbon atoms, linked in hexagons.
Inside a sheet the bonds are **strong.** Between sheets, they're **weak.**
Inside each sheet the atoms hold on tight. Between the sheets, the forces are weak.
So the sheets **slip** over each other, like a deck of cards.
So the sheets slip over each other, like cards sliding off a deck.
In 1795, Conté mixed graphite powder with **clay.**
In 1795, Nicolas-Jacques Conté found a way to mix graphite powder with clay.
More clay: a **harder** core and a **lighter** mark.
More clay makes the core harder, and the mark lighter.
**H** for hardness, **B** for blackness. Yours is **HB.**
That's the code printed on the side. H for hardness, B for blackness. Your everyday pencil is HB.
In the factory, graphite and clay are mixed **with water.**
In the factory, graphite and clay are mixed with water.
The paste becomes **long strings,** dried and fired in a **kiln.**
The paste is shaped into long, spaghetti-like strings, then dried, cut, and fired in a kiln.
Each core sits in a **grooved wooden slat.** A second slat is **glued** on top.
Each core is laid in a grooved slat of wood, and a second slat is glued on top.
The wood keeps the core from **breaking,** and off your hand.
The wood protects the core from breaking, and keeps it from marking your hand.
Now **drag the tip** across paper.
Now drag the tip across paper.
The tip **wears away,** leaving a **trail of graphite.**
The tip wears away by rubbing, and leaves a trail of graphite on the page.
No ink at all. Just **sheets of carbon** left behind.
No ink at all. Just sheets of carbon, left behind.
Over **14 billion** pencils are made every year.
Over fourteen billion pencils are made around the world every year.
